items.summary: Security disposition: evidence_needed. Risk severity is high for new public exposure and security-sensitive releases because fleet-doctor has no run or findings, operations has no deploy/uptime/error sweep results, and security sitefacts are unknown for all 61 managed sites. Authentication and access boundaries, secrets handling, container isolation, release controls, dependency provenance, data exposure, monitoring, incident readiness, and security.txt/disclosure readiness remain unevidenced. No compromise evidence is present. TLS has no reported certificates expiring within 30 days, but complete TLS configuration is unknown. Compliance is a technical baseline only: 36 pass, 19 fail, and 6 unknown. Exact decision: keep private-launch and security-sensitive release gates unchanged; permit only existing reversible growth that adds no credentials, permissions, dependencies, data collection, or cross-site behavior and passes existing checks. Do not claim certification or a clean bill of health.

Continue the existing consolidated fleet security evidence matrix using authorized metadata and retained artifacts only. Record dated evidence, explicit unknowns, affected scope, owners, severity, and release implications for authentication/access boundaries, secrets exposure, container isolation, release/deploy controls, dependency and supply-chain provenance, TLS configuration, data exposure, monitoring and incident signals, and security.txt/disclosure readiness. Do not retrieve credentials, access private containers, exploit targets, modify permissions or configuration, add dependencies, deploy, expand data collection, or request duplicate telemetry.

Ordinary reversible growth is conditionally permissible and is not blocked solely for optional hardening. The existing allthingsmasonic.com CTA refinement may proceed only after capacity clears and existing validation passes, preserving the registered destination and tracking ID allthingsmasonic-20, adjacent disclosure, accessibility, responsive behavior, link validation, and single-diff rollback. This is not security-sensitive release or public-launch clearance.
